[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was baptised at Kilwinning on 19 December 1703. The retained Findmypast transcript names his parents as John Glasgow and Jean Wylie and gives residence Chappell. The baptism date does not by itself establish an exact birthday.<ref>[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3625663&tab=this Findmypast,SCOT/OPR/BAP/3625663], Kilwinning,19 December 1703; previously validated transcript. Compare ScotlandsPeople OPR 599,10/131.</ref>

The named parents are represented by [[Glasgow-1065|John Glasgow]] and [[Wyllie-1044|Jean Wyllie]]. The older father reference Glasgow-2463 is preserved in the previous biography below. This child is provisionally compared with [[Glasgow-2467|John Glasgow, husband of Mary Auld]], father of Andrew and James at Kilwinning in 1746 and 1750. Their identity remains uncertain; the profiles are not merged and no adult event is newly proved for this child.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1065]] is assessed at 88% (probable). John’s 19 December 1703 Chappell baptism names John Glasgow and Jean Wylie, matching father-1065’s recurring adult Wyllie household. The selected father account is also the 1683 child, whose continuity to this adult is compatible at about 20 but unproved.

Literal adult father99%; complete selected edge includes the 1683-child-to-Wyllie-husband identification. The child’s later Mary Auld identity is separate.

Next useful test: Seek the Wyllie marriage and original 1703/1683 entries for household links, distinguishing the maternal 1683 index conflict.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3625663&tab=this Findmypast, Kilwinning John baptism 19 December 1703, John Glasgow/Jean Wylie, Chappell, SCOT/OPR/BAP/3625663; previously validated transcript]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1065|John Glasgow, Jean Wyllie household]] is selected as the uncertain working father of [[Glasgow-2467|John Glasgow, Mary Auld household]], the John recorded with Mary Auld at Kilwinning for Andrew’s baptism on 26 October 1746 and James’s on 19 August 1750. The later John’s existing biography already suggests descent from [[Glasgow-2463|Glasgow-2463]], an old parent reference with a 16 September 1683 Kilwinning date. The current captured family fields of the older household’s children point to [[Glasgow-1065|John Glasgow, Jean Wyllie household]], whose profile carries that same 1683 date and the Jean Wyllie household. This resolves the intended candidate account; it is not a new historical father statement. A specific route is the recorded [[Glasgow-2464|John Glasgow, Kilwinning child of 1703]], baptised at Kilwinning on 19 December 1703 to John Glasgow and Jean Wylie, residence Chappell. Treat that child provisionally as the later Mary Auld husband. If baptised in infancy, he would have been about 42 and 46 at the two known children’s baptisms, compatible ages for a father. The later profile’s before-1728 estimate permits this earlier birth. Exact name, parish, an already recorded descent suggestion and a documented child with named parents give a testable family model. No record yet establishes that the child and adult were the same man.

[[Wyllie-1044|Jean Wyllie / Wylie]] is separately selected as the uncertain working mother through the same possible 1703-child identity. The 1703 index actually names Jean Wylie; she is not supplied merely because she is the selected father’s wife. Her existing profile also cites the 1712 Margaret and 1715 Matthew entries in the same household. The circa-1682 birth is an estimate, and the records cited here do not supply a marriage date or prove her age. Her identification as mother of the Mary Auld husband remains dependent on that adult’s identification with the 1703 child. The two parent fields therefore represent one conditional family connection, not two independent confirmations.

The existing child-record citations are Kilwinning OPR 599, 10/131 for John in 1703, 20/93 for Andrew in 1746, and 20/106 for James in 1750. The retained Findmypast transcript SCOT/OPR/BAP/3625663 names the 1703 parents and residence Chappell. No original register image has been newly inspected. The baptism does not establish an exact birthday. [[Glasgow-2468|Glasgow-2468]] and [[Glasgow-2469|Glasgow-2469]] retain their existing father and Mary Auld retains her existing spouse and maternal links; no new certainty is assigned to them. The 1703 child and later father remain separate profile accounts, possibly duplicates rather than two proved brothers. No merge is performed, and no vital field changes to 1703 follow from this model.

The older John’s profile also represents a Kilwinning baptism on 16 September 1683. If those child and later-father identities are correct, he was about twenty at the 1703 baptism. This is compatible, but not independent proof that the 1683 child became Jean Wyllie’s husband. The competing Jean Gardiner and Jonet Young mother names in the 1683 indexes remain unresolved, as do the older account’s existing ancestral qualifications. A later son of the Wyllie household, a grandson through a different child, or another local Glasgow father remains possible for [[Glasgow-2467|John Glasgow, Mary Auld household]]. The already recorded descent suggestion does not specify a generation. The 1703-child route is selected because it provides a named child in the right parish with feasible later fatherhood, without inventing an intermediate ancestor; it is preferred only weakly.

The nearby Stevenston [[Glasgow-4170|Glasgow-4170]] and Mary Auld-2246 household, documented for Margaret in 1717 and Euphan in 1718, is an alternative family to compare, not an established identity with the Kilwinning John and Mary Auld-1724. Matching the mother’s name does not change the father’s recorded forename or prove that the women were the same person. No new half-sibling, remarriage or widowhood is asserted. Missing corroboration does not exclude either childhood or household comparison. Another Kilwinning John could have fathered Andrew and James. The present model should be tested against the original 1703, 1746 and 1750 residences, witnesses and any marriage entry.

One uncertain father and one uncertain mother are selected through one possible child-to-adult identity. No original inspection, merge, new certainty or live WikiTree edit is claimed. Existing dates, recorded family fields and the 1683 mother-name disagreement remain intact. Working connectivity counts retained profile accounts, including possible duplicates; it is not a count of proved distinct people or independent discoveries.
